calculation.method: WGS84 ellipsoidal segment lengths (Vincenty inverse) and geodesic interpolation along the supplied main polyline; first crossing found by bisection. Historic gold pin is projected onto its nearest route segment.
calculation.displayRecommendation: Show approximate distances to 0.1 km or whole kilometres. Numerical precision is for drawing the same source line, not a navigation guarantee.

timing.elapsedHoursFormula: routeKm / chosen overall average km per hour (including breaks)
timing.note: Any displayed times must be clearly labelled user-selected scenarios. Confirm the event start separately; do not imply live progress or official checkpoint times.

uncertainties: This is the main polyline from the 2025 map, not a confirmed 2026 route or live tracker.

The KML also contains ten short alternative/correction lines. They are not stitched into the main route because their replacement intent is not encoded; small route changes will shift milestone locations.
Town names are general meeting zones. Route milestones are not town centres, parking permissions or official checkpoints.
The original route has not been rechecked for current access, diversions, pavement continuity or road conditions; show it as a route overview rather than turn-by-turn navigation.
Gold is 60 miles from Meriden as the crow flies, not 60 miles walked. The approximate Cross coordinate and the route-start vertex differ slightly; only the current official tracker determines gold.
The historic gold target is an optional planning endpoint with a small distance margin; it is not a designated event finish or parking place.

New 110, 120 and 123 km reference dots are interpolated along the 2025 source line. They do not imply three new support car parking stops. The nearest source meeting choices are existing numbered Points 18–23.

historicGoldPlanningEnd.context: Jeff’s historical gold pin; not the current support planning end
